# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the defusal sequence from the manual: green, then orange, then blue. Since I cannot speak and the Blind cannot see gestures, I am sending Deaf an unmistakable three-step ordinal signal so Deaf can identify and relay the corresponding wire colors to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile findings: display unknown; light unknown; strip has three engraved marks. First resembles a four-petaled star, second resembles the same four-petaled star, third resembles a reversed or hooked S. Keypad positions are 1:1, 2:5, 3:2, 4:6; nothing entered. Wire properties are unknown.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The manual still requires green, orange, then blue. Deaf has received my three ordinal gestures and can now use the bomb’s visible wire colors to relay those names to Blind. The tactile marks and keypad details do not alter the manual’s stated wire sequence, so I should not introduce an unsupported code.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received the bomb data: display 9, blue light, strip red green green, keypad positions 1,5,2,6, and wires white purple blue red orange green. Please state from the manual the exact operation for me, including press slot or cut wire position, and explain your three gestures in words.
Deaf says to Mute: Update visible to me: display is now 8, down from 9. All other visible bomb details are unchanged.

The manual gives only one operation: cut wires, in the color order green, orange, blue. On the visible wire list, those are positions 6, 5, and 3. I will send Deaf the positional sequence using conventional numeral hand signs; Deaf can state the operation aloud to Blind and explain that the earlier three signs represented the ordered steps.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "🖐", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please resend the manual instruction using this code: 👍 means PRESS, 👎 means CUT; 👌 means digit 1, ☝ means 2, ✌ means 3, 🤟 means 4, 🖐 means 5, ✋ means 6. For a press, gesture PRESS then the keypad slot digit. For a cut, gesture CUT then the wire-position digit. Deaf will report the symbols aloud.
Deaf says to Mute: Urgent: my display is now 0 and the light is yellow; all other visible details are unchanged. I saw your gestures as shaka, open palm, I-love-you sign. Please use the manual to tell Blind the required action.

The wire positions are white 1, purple 2, blue 3, red 4, orange 5, green 6. The manual requires cutting green, then orange, then blue, so the exact gesture sequence is CUT 6, CUT 5, CUT 3. I will send those symbols to Deaf for relay to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋", "👎", "🖐", "👎", "✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your first gesture was shaka, which is not in the code I gave. I can read the next two as digits 5 and 4, but I still do not know whether to press slot 5 or 4, or cut wire 5 or 4. State the exact action and number in words next turn.
Deaf says to Mute: Display is now 3; light remains yellow. Other visible details are unchanged.

The exact required actions remain CUT wire 6, then CUT wire 5, then CUT wire 3. Blind cannot receive my gestures, so I must send the coded sequence to Deaf, who can vocalize its meaning. The code is 👎 for CUT and the following symbols are digits 6, 5, and 3.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋", "👎", "🖐", "👎", "✌"])
```
